speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we will set aside the resources to advance this important agenda.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Importantly, no one in Singapore will be denied access to appropriate care because of an inability to pay.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members also spoke about private insurance coverage outside of healthcare, including in areas like life insurance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Life insurers in Singapore have, in fact, offered coverage to persons with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the underwriting of such persons can be a complex matter, as our own data is limited and insurers here typically reference the underwriting guidelines of global life reinsurers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will study and review how this coverage can be improved and ensure that financial institutions deal fairly with all their customers, including those with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Importantly, we will have a bigger focus on preventive care, so that everyone can take proactive steps and take charge of their own mental health.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want our children to develop good cyber habits, so they learn to use the Internet and social media safely and responsibly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To be clear, our approach is not to remove all stress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is not going to help our children.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, we want our children to learn to deal with stress at age-appropriate levels.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want them to develop self-belief and resilience and grow up with the confidence to tackle challenges, stresses and demands that they will surely encounter later in life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to integrate mental well-being into our Healthier SG and other preventive health programmes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We sometimes think of body and mind as separate entities, but they are closely linked, each affecting the other greatly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Staying active; exercising regularly; connecting with friends in person, not online; learning new skills; contributing to a larger purpose.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All these sound like commonsensical advice, but they are not so easy to do and they are foundational habits that will enable all of us to improve our overall well-being.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But for all these plans to work, we also need to change our attitudes and mindsets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We need to do more to destigmatise mental health conditions so that people do not hesitate to seek help.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Stigma reduces a complex and difficult problem into unhelpful labels and stereotypes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It opens people struggling with mental health to discrimination, such as in the job market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It may cause them to be socially ostracised.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It makes them feel ashamed, isolated and stops them from seeking treatment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As I mentioned just now, we do see attitudes shifting.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the stigma remains and we can do much more to build a society where we help one another cope with life's stressors, are considerate of one another's feelings and carve out safe spaces for them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also need to change our mindsets about what we consider success in life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is good to have a culture in Singapore that values hard work, promotes excellence and encourages everyone to aspire and strive to do better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we should not be unwittingly drawn into a rat race of hypercompetition and endless comparisons with one another just to get ahead of others, but end up worse off as a society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, this was one of the key points from our Forward Singapore engagements.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The vast majority of Singaporeans wish to see a more inclusive Singapore Dream.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One where we are not pressured to conform to narrow definitions of success, where we embrace excellence and talents across many different areas and find meaning and purpose in what we do.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we cannot make this happen through policy alone.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our attitudes, our mindsets must also change and align with our shared aspirations for a refreshed Singapore Dream.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, to achieve all of these goals, we must work together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are many ground-up initiatives and community and social services organisations already working in different ways to meet the mental health and well-being needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I know from personal experience, having served as Patron to the Samaritans of Singapore for more than 10 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I have interacted with many of the volunteers there and seen first-hand, their commitment and dedication to save lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We value the collaborations and partnerships with all of you.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I call on all Singaporeans, who are passionate about this issue of mental health and well-being, to join us in this national movement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have lots to do and a full agenda ahead of us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the issues are complex and we do not have all the answers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want everyone on board, so we learn together and continue to finetune our strategies based on your feedback and ideas and our shared experiences and insights.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Together, let us build a Singapore where everyone matters, where everyone has a place and where everyone belongs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Together, hand-in-hand, let us improve the mental health and well-being of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: He highlighted an important starting point in our approach: that mental health issues lie on a spectrum and that, this means we need a broad suite of solutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This means that while individuals may experience symptoms of poor mental health, they may be due to transient stressors and do not necessarily warrant the same intensity of interventions needed for individuals diagnosed with mental disorders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Receiving care in the community as the first line of support, rather than at hospitals, is therefore, more appropriate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The cornerstone of our National Mental Health and Well-Being Strategy is the tiered care model.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It sets the foundation for how our mental health services should be organised, with different care levels, depending on the intensity of interventions needed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This, ultimately, helps us to provide the right care at the right time, based on the individual's needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Right-siting of care to the community is part of a much larger shift of mental health care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Countries, like Australia, Canada and the United Kingdom (UK), have implemented a similar model for their mental health care systems.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Although more research studies are still being done, existing studies suggest that a tiered model of mental health care delivery, where mental health care can be easily accessible in community settings, is a better approach compared to concentrating services in the hospital settings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Senior Minister of State for Health will speak more on our tiered care model later.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For the tiered care model to be effective, we also need to encourage the right mindsets, allocate resources and build support within the community to empower people.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I will, therefore, be addressing the mental health promotion efforts, community mental well-being initiatives, the affordability of mental health services as well as the manpower needs in providing mental health care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As shared by Dr Wan Rizal when he spoke on the importance of mental health literacy, raising awareness on mental health is crucial in shifting our societal values and attitudes towards making mental well-being, one of our priorities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have made progress in this area as we see improvement in the public's attitudes towards individuals with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, we recognise that stigma around mental health issues persist in our society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our efforts include encouraging help-seeking, reducing stigma and discrimination against people with mental health conditions through public campaigns and targeted initiatives for youths, seniors, caregivers, women, persons with disabilities and minorities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At the national level, HPB's "It's OKAY to Reach Out" campaign and NCSS' Beyond the Label movement, aim to normalise conversations around mental health and encourage help-seeking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These efforts are sustained through social media outreach and online portals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: HPB's MindSG offers mental health resources, curated by professionals, including tools for users to assess their mental health risks and search for support or services, based on their needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The portal will be enhanced, progressively, to introduce more topics and features.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In schools, HPB offers training for students going through critical transition years, specifically from Primary 6 to Secondary 1.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These programmes are carried out in partnership with schools, to equip students with skills to better cope through these transitions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Additionally, in 2023, HPB has trained more than 2,200 students from IHLs as peer supporters, equipping them with empathetic listening and basic mental health first-aid skills.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At workplaces, HPB trains management staff and conducts workshops to enable people to better cope at work and support their colleagues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In 2023, more than 55,000 working adults have benefitted from HPB's mental wellness programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Besides HPB-led initiatives, the Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) Council also launched the "Take Time to Take Care" campaign, to remind employees to look after their own and their colleagues' well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In the community, Well-Being Circles have been established across various neighbourhoods to raise awareness on mental health, the available resources and to empower citizens with skills to look after their own mental well-being as well as that of others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to encourage the formation of more Well-Being Circles, so that more in the community will have access to the support when they need it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Apart from community-wide efforts in mental health promotion, there are also several initiatives that target specific groups.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: According to the 2022 National Population Health Survey, youths aged 18 to 29 years old formed the largest proportion of people with poor mental health in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Currently, we have community mental health teams, known as Community Outreach Teams (CREST)-Youth and Youth Integrated Teams (YITs), dedicated to support youths with mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: CREST-Youth, reaches out to youths and parents to promote early identification of mental health symptoms and provide basic emotional support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: YITs, carry out mental health assessments and provide psychosocial interventions for youths who need more intensive support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In addition to these community mental health teams, the Response, Early Intervention and Assessment in Community Mental Health (REACH) teams work closely with schools to provide mental health assessments and interventions, for students aged six to 19 years old.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To support youths at risk of suicide or severe self-harm, an intermediate residential facility will also be developed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Not all youths who present with suicidal behaviour, suffer from mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Instead, they may have experienced social stressors, such as having difficulties coping with schoolwork and being bullied.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Therefore, this facility will cater to this group of youths, aged 10 to 19 years old, to support them within a safe environment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In the facility, youths will be supported by a multi-disciplinary team, consisting of psychiatrists, psychologists, social workers, nurses and live-in care staff.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Services provided will include: identifying the needs of youths in crisis; providing psychosocial interventions, such as counselling and supportive medical attention, where necessary; and, facilitating the transition of youths with support from community partners before they are discharged.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In the course of supporting the mental health of our youths, there have been ground feedback on the need for parental consent for children and youths below 21 years old, which could hinder their access to mental health support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We recognise the importance of our youths' continued access to mental health services, and I appreciate Miss Rachel Ong's earlier suggestion, of having tiered guidelines for the requirement of parental consent on mental health services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In this regard, I would like to lay out several considerations that MOH is reviewing as we navigate this issue.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These include, balancing the need for youths' access to appropriate treatment; the involvement of the family and social support in youths' care journey; protection of the youths in view of the risks associated with treatments; and the level of maturity and understanding of the child.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Above all, our priority, is to ensure that any approach taken is in the best interest of the child and that they can receive timely mental health care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are studying this issue and exploring meaningful options to address it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Several Members, like Mr Yip Hon Weng and Ms Nadia Samdin, spoke about the need to do more to support our seniors with mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Currently, seniors are supported by CREST, to identify their mental health needs and provide basic emotional support and referrals to appropriate service providers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In addition, Active Ageing Centres work with CREST providers, in serving as community nodes, to conduct activities that engage and connect seniors within the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have 73 CREST teams island-wide, of which, 65 teams can support seniors at-risk of mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We understand that some seniors may be reluctant to seek help or accept support for their mental health needs, due to stigma.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As part of their outreach efforts, the Silver Generation Ambassadors who come across these seniors would also share about mental health resources in the community and encourage them to seek help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are glad that there are also community initiatives, carried out by Members in their constituencies, that reach out to these seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are also looking at mental well-being issues of our seniors and tackling the social phenomenon of loneliness, as part of the holistic Age Well SG strategy, announced last November.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For caregivers, who have or are at risk of developing depression, anxiety and burnout, due to their caregiving role, CREST can provide dedicated support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These teams support caregivers in self-care, stress management and future planning, such as making a Lasting Power of Attorney and Advanced Care Planning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Where necessary, they will also link caregivers with counselling services and peer support groups, like the Caregiver Support Network.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) also administers the Caregiver Training Grant, which provides subsidies for caregiver training, including psychosocial management of behavioural issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For caregivers, who need short-term support to have their loved ones taken care of, some MOH-funded psychiatric nursing homes offer the Nursing Home Respite Care programme, which provides eligible clients with short periods of stay – typically ranging from a week to a month.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Such arrangements, allow caregivers some time off, with the assurance that their loved ones are safely cared for in the nursing home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Several efforts are ongoing to support the mental health of women.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, the National University Hospital (NUH) Women's Emotional Health Services (WEHS), provides both antenatal and postnatal mental health screening as well as individualised treatment interventions, for women who need more support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The NUH WEHS team, also works closely with community partners and social service providers to coordinate and provide continuity of care to those who need it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Similarly, the Postnatal Depression Intervention Programme in KK Women's and Children's Hospital (KKH), provides routine post-natal depression screening for all pregnant women; and those with depressive symptoms will be referred to the appropriate services available.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mental health services, including mental health screening for mothers, are also available in polyclinics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To support fathers and spouses, NUH will be extending its mental health screening to support them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The programme allows for early intervention, case management and multi-disciplinary treatment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In 2020, the KKH Psychosocial Trauma Support Service also began providing trauma-focused assessments and interventions to women experiencing psycho-emotional difficulties that arose from traumatic incidents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH is committed to working with partners to deliver holistic care for PwDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To address their healthcare needs, MOH works with community partners to provide the Home Personal Care service, which offers a range of services, including assistance with personal hygiene, housekeeping and simple maintenance exercises.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Over the past years, we have also collaborated with the College of Family Physicians Singapore to offer a Family Practice Skills Course to equip general practitioners in caring for persons with intellectual disabilities; and, piloted a Community Integrated Health Team, in partnership with a social service agency; as well as, a specialist outreach team from IMH, to offer home- or community-based care for persons with intellectual disabilities, who have complex health needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to build these capabilities in the community to support more caregivers and families of PwDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In the Malay/Muslim community, we have organisations, like Club Heal, which has championed mental health issues for years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I lead M3's Focus Area on Community Health, which was introduced last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: M3 is a collaboration between the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS), MENDAKI and Malay Activity Executive Committees Council (MESRA).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The newly introduced Focus Area on Community Health, aims to promote healthy lifestyles and empower residents to spearhead ground-up efforts, within their own community – including efforts on mental health and well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In towns, like M3@Jalan Besar, youth peer support groups have been set up and the community is rallied to co-create solutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to roll out such initiatives, to enhance residents' mental well-being in the different towns.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are fortunate to have organisations, like Club Heal, which has championed this issue for many years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is important that we continue to reinforce these efforts and garner more support from the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As part of the National Mental Health and Well-Being Strategy, efforts are being undertaken to ensure that support and initiatives are readily available in our community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I currently lead the M3 Focus Area on community health and well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This new Focus Area aims to promote a healthy lifestyle and empower residents to spearhead efforts in their own communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: One cornerstone of this endeavour is addressing mental health and mental well-being issues in our community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I welcome efforts being done at the towns such as M3@Jalan Besar led by Dr Wan Rizal.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Peer support groups for youths have been set up and the community is invited to co-create solutions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to implement such initiatives to improve the mental well-being of residents across Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: (In English): Let me touch on the affordability of mental health services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In this regard, we have made efforts to reduce out-of-pocket costs through various schemes available.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These subsidies are available at public specialist outpatient clinics, polyclinics and participating GP clinics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For patients aged 60 years and above, they can use an additional $300 each year from their Flexi-MediSave to offset out-of-pocket payments for their outpatient mental health treatment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Patients may also receive subsidised or free counselling services provided by various community service providers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For inpatient services, all Singaporeans and Permanent Residents are covered under MediShield Life, regardless of preexisting conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MediShield Life and MediSave claim limits are regularly refreshed to ensure that they remain sufficient to cover nine in 10 subsidised bills.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: On top of MediShield Life, Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and other private health insurance plans may provide additional coverage for mental health treatment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, all IP insurers offer plans that cover in-patient mental health treatment and the amount of coverage is decided by the insurers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For lower-income Singaporeans who require more financial assistance to pay for their remaining healthcare bills, they may apply for MediFund, which serves as a safety net for needy Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I share Dr Tan Wu Meng's concern regarding denied access to private insurance for persons with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Several other Members have also raised this concern.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This should be considered within the larger context of our healthcare financing system where all Singaporeans are eligible for subsidies and are covered under MediShield Life, which is a national risk pool that helps to ensure its sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: On the other hand, IPs and other private health insurance products are optional.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Private insurers may exclude pre-existing conditions from coverage upon underwriting, including mental health conditions, informed by actuarial and commercial considerations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Such a process allows insurers to ensure their risk pool remains sustainable, as they, otherwise, have to increase premiums for all policyholders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Depending on their underwriting assessment frameworks, insurers may still offer coverage to applicants with pre-existing conditions but with exclusions or higher premiums.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It allows this group of applicants to still benefit from some coverage without adversely affecting other policyholders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Notwithstanding, MOH and the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) fully expect all insurers to deal fairly with their customers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Insurers are expected to carry out an objective assessment of every application based on reliable information or data relevant to the risks being insured.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Insurers should not indiscriminately reject an application solely on the basis of declared personal information, including mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Where an application is rejected or approved with higher premiums or additional conditions, insurers should properly explain to the customer the basis for the underwriting decision.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH and MAS take this seriously, and MAS will take action against insurers whose practices are in breach of its regulations or guidance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I also thank Dr Tan Wu Meng for highlighting the Forum Letter by Ms Tan Hui In.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MAS does not have records of her feedback in its complaints database.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: If Dr Tan Wu Meng has additional information to share about this specific case, he can share it with MAS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Then, MAS can promptly look into it with the relevant insurers, if the complainant consents to it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Members of the public with similar feedback can also write to MAS and MAS will investigate accordingly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: On the feedback on long waiting times to access mental health treatment services, MOH will, similarly, look into the issue.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: One of the key considerations is the adequacy of mental health professionals, including psychiatrists and psychologists.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As of 2022, there were 203 registered psychiatrists and 212 psychologists in the public sector.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, solely increasing the number of psychiatrists and psychologists will be insufficient and unsustainable to meet increasing demands for mental health services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is also one of the reasons why we have developed the tiered care model.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With the tiered care model, more patients will receive timely care in the community, provided by appropriate mental health professionals, such as counsellors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I am encouraged by the efforts and progress we are making, as a nation, in tackling this extremely important and challenging area.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In particular, we have made advancements in integrating various aspects of our social, education and health sectors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To illustrate, let me share the story of Mr Chee Soon Weng.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chee was an experienced teacher and managed students with challenging behavioural issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This took a toll on his mental health and over time, he suffered from comorbid anxiety and depressive disorder.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As a result, Mr Chee transited from a student-facing role to an administrative and research position at work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At home, he also encountered issues with his family due to his mood.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: He then approached the Methodist Welfare Service's FSC under the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), who identified his mental health needs and referred him to one of our COMIT Anglican Care Centre teams for support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through weekly counselling and psychoeducation on symptoms and treatment plans, Mr Chee made significant progress in his mental health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, Mr Chee is coping well with his new position at work and his relationship with his family has also improved.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chee's story underscores the importance of integrating social service and health sectors to enhance mental health care for individuals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In closing, I would like to record my gratitude to Members who have raised this Motion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It has given us the opportunity to highlight the mental health efforts that we have developed and implemented through the years, as well as hear various feedback and suggestions on how we can do more.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I would also like to take this opportunity to thank all our community service providers for their unwavering dedication and their instrumental role in implementing these initiatives on the ground.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As mentioned by the Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu Mahzam, the tiered care model is the foundation of our National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These services target different levels of mental health needs – from community-led mental health promotion, self-help and peer support at Tier 1, to the most intensive level of care in hospitals and specialist clinics at Tier 4 of our tiered care model.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: There are also many ground-up initiatives across sectors, such as those under the Beyond the Label Collective, to address the mental health and well-being needs of our people and reduce stigma.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These services and ground-up initiatives serve as the foundation of our work, building upon the larger National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In spite of our vibrant mental health services landscape, we have heard feedback, however, that help-seeking can be overwhelming as many do not know where, when and how to seek help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is a key issue for us, as there remains a treatment gap.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many who need help are not getting the help that they need; and far too many get help far later than they should.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The complex web of services available can, indeed, have the unintended consequence of deterring help-seeking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We want to make it easy for anyone to seek help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: No going at it alone or figuring out your way by yourself.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will set up first-stop touchpoints; essentially "go-to places" for mental health support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our first-stop touchpoints will identify their clients' mental health needs and provide the appropriate service.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This can mean relevant information, immediate mental health support and intervention, or referrals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For example, callers and texters with no or minimal mental health needs and want to learn well-being skills can be referred to Well-being Circles in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On the other end of the spectrum, those with suicidal tendencies may be connected to the Samaritans of Singapore's (SOS') Hotline and Care Text for support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Two, a digital platform, such as Mindline or MindSG.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It does not matter which resource users visit first, since both link to each other.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Both websites contain curated content by mental health experts, self-assessment tools and links to other resources, including our in-person touchpoints for mental health support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mindline also has an online forum named "Ask a Therapist", where users can engage with verified professionals and a Wysa AI-enabled chatbot, where users can share their emotions safely and anonymously without the fear of being judged, anywhere and anytime.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will build up and promote in-person touchpoints, including community mental health teams such as CREST, as in-person first-stop touchpoints, so that the public knows where to seek help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With this move, we hope that the public will become more aware of the existence of the many social service agencies in our community providing psychotherapy and emotional support and not just clinics and hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In the course of their work, social service professionals often encounter clients with unmet mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In fact, many may not recognise that they are in need of mental health support themselves.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For our 500 frontline staff across our Social Service Offices, we plan to train them in psychological first aid.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also intend to train another 1,000 frontline social service professionals to be capable of identifying mental health concerns, provide casework and counselling and refer clients to appropriate services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These social service professionals will be trained by 2030.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Directing clients to appropriate services at the get-go does not mean the job is done.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: An individual's mental health needs can change over time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To provide a seamless care experience for clients, service providers across the social service and health sectors need to work ever closer together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, different providers have different screening, assessment, collaboration, referral, IT and data-sharing practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The practice guide will help to better ensure that clients are referred to and receive mental health resources or interventions appropriate to their needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: When their needs change, the support for them can be adjusted accordingly, that is, stepped up to higher-intensity services or stepped down to lower-intensity services, as needed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: While there are good examples of collaboration and coordination across social service and healthcare sectors today, not all cases are handled in a systematic and consistent manner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To help raise overall practice standards and the experience for those seeking help, the practice guide will clearly lay out the kinds of services different agencies in the social and health sector should provide and how they should work with one another to serve clients with mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At the end of the day, it is all about serving individuals with mental health support needs better.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, we hope that any Singaporean in need of mental health support will not have to navigate their help-seeking journey alone and as a result, feel lost or afraid.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Seeking help should not be a lonely experience.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Further, social service professionals often encounter individuals with mental health needs in the course of their work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many of these individuals may not even be aware of their own mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: There is only one ultimate goal: to provide more comprehensive and client-centric services for Singaporeans with mental health needs. : Mr Speaker, our mission at hand is one that is salient and pressing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our national mental health strategy lays the foundation and gives us direction so that we can collectively get to a better place in terms of our mental health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Beyond plans, policies and programmes, perhaps, more importantly so, we need a further shift in mindsets surrounding mental health and people with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Much has been done, but more work remains.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With the help of Members of this Chamber from both sides of the aisle and beyond, I have every confidence that Singapore can be a paragon where stigma surrounding mental health is a thing of the past and where help-seeking is well-facilitated.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Many adults spend substantial time at work and, sometimes, work can be stressful and affect one's mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It is, thus, important that we look at how workplaces can support mental well-being of employees and what each of us can do to create kinder, more inclusive workplaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I will, first, touch on the plans to support general mental well-being of employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is a community of practice for Well-being Champions to exchange best practices and access more resources and training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Who are these Well-being Champions, you might ask?

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: A Well-being Champion is typically a management-level employee or individual whom the company empowers to lead the well-being agenda and implement mental well-being measures in the company.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: One such Well-being Champion, who has joined the Network, is Mr Hon Lip Yung, General Manager of a local SME.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Network allows Mr Hon to learn from Well-being Champions of other companies on how they implement mental well-being initiatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Hon is now looking forward to attending training with other members in this Network, which is aligned to Tier 1 of the National Competency Training Framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will work closely with the various Government agencies, tripartite partners and trade associations to expand the network.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Peer support is another important part of strengthening workplace mental well-being support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: NCSS and HPB are working together to enhance training for peer supporters and develop a framework to support them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The peer supporters would be equipped to provide emotional support and lend a listening ear to colleagues at the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I agree with Mr Edward Chia's suggestion that every company should have a framework to support their employees' well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Employers may refer to the Playbook on Workplace Mental Well-being for step-by-step guidance to implement mental well-being initiatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: HR leaders play an important role in this ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I encourage more HR professionals to join the Mental Well-being Champions Network.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Institute of Human Resource Professionals (IHRP) has also established the Body of Competencies for HR professionals, which identifies the execution of employee benefits, including mental well-being initiatives, as an expected functional competency for HR professionals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) will continue to partner IHRP to equip and support the HR industry on this front.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I agree with Mr Mark Lee and other Members on the importance of both physical and mental health.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is why MOM and the WSH Council take a Total WSH approach to workers' well-being, focusing on both physical and mental health.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: On Mr Ong Hua Han's interest in the support for SMEs, the Total WSH programme provides SMEs with free access to qualified consultants who can advise them on how to manage safety and health in an integrated way and provide intervention programmes, such as mental well-being workshops.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have streamlined the administrative overheads for SMEs to participate more easily and fully.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I agree with Mr Edward Chia that it is important for a company to measure the state of mental well-being of its employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Companies can use MOM's iWorkHealth assessment tool, which is a free online, company-administered tool to better understand their employees' state of mental well-being, including the workplace stressors that the employees are facing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Edward Chia also suggested harmonising the iWorkHealth tool with the Human Capital Diagnostic Tool.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We need to balance between harmonising tools for ease and gaining an overview of the organisation's environment and workforce, while ensuring that the tools and surveys are kept functional, purposeful and at a reasonable length for the employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Carrie Tan and Mr Melvin Yong also suggested introducing the "Right to Disconnect", sometimes, known as after-hours work communication policy to people.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Guidance on how to implement such a policy is in the Tripartite Advisory on Mental Health and Well-being at Workplaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will continue to work with our tripartite partners, including NTUC and the Singapore National Employers' Federation, to raise awareness of the importance of setting after-hours work communication policy while managing both employees' and business needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: At the same time, the tripartite partners are pushing for greater adoption of work-life harmony measures, such as health and wellness programmes and unrecorded time-off for personal and family matters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I share Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Darryl David, Mr Vikram Nair and Mr Ong Hua Han's call in getting more companies to subscribe to the EAP.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Employers may refer to the refreshed EAP service providers list in the Tripartite Advisory, which includes EAP service providers offering subsidised rates and details of their offerings, such as indicative pricings and areas of specialisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Apart from EAP services, individuals experiencing mental distress or just needing a listening ear, can tap on the new National Mental Health Hotline and Text Service from 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: There are also free online resources, such as Belle the helpbot and Mindline.sg.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Jean See will be happy to note that self-employed individuals and freelancers can tap on such free resources, too.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I note Ms Hazel Poa and Assoc Prof Razwana Begum's suggestion for a four-day work week.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: However, as with any work arrangement, this may only work well for certain sectors and jobs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I encourage employers to proactively discuss with employees the types of FWAs that suit both their business context and their employees' specific needs, including for caregivers who might have special needs, as mentioned by Ms Yeo Wan Ling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Supportive companies that demonstrate exemplary mental well-being practices can be recognised through the annual WSH Culture of Acceptance, Respect and Empathy Award.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I acknowledge Ms Ng Ling Ling, Ms Mariam Jaafar and other Members' concern for the mental health of our young adults, especially for those adjusting to their first careers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The National Youth Council's Mentoring SG Movement provides accessible mentoring programmes to support youths in managing life transitions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Young NTUC is one of our partners which has put in place several initiatives, such as career preparation workshops for youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This includes providing a range of well-being programmes and resources to equip them with the skills and knowledge for self-care; joining the Well-being Champions Network; having a whole-of-Government confidential counselling services hotline for public officers to speak to trained counsellors; and building a community of Wellness Ambassadors, who are trained peer supporters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Public Service will continue to strengthen support for our public officers' mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I will now cover how we are supporting the employment and employability of individuals with mental health conditions who are on recovery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Keith Chua has suggested stronger support for individuals with mental health conditions who are looking for a job.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To drive inclusivity in training, SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) is working with training providers to raise awareness of mental health and well-being in adult learners, develop customised training courses and increase accessibility of some mainstream courses to cater to trainees with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For those who require customised employment support, agencies, such as IMH, the Singapore Anglican Community Services and the Singapore Association for Mental Health provide services to place them with suitable employers, advise employers on job task adaptations and train supervisors to better support these employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: One such company is Konica Minolta, which has partnered the IMH Job Club since 2016 to recruit individuals in recovery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: They are paired with a peer buddy and the company works closely with IMH to effect workplace adjustments, such as moderating their workload and tasks to a more suitable pace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Through the joint support by IMH and the employer, these individuals gain and sustain meaningful employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We are looking to help employment support agencies expand their partnerships with trade associations and chambers, to encourage more companies to come onboard to hire and retain employees recovering from mental health conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It is difficult to calibrate salary support to cater to fluctuations in the conditions of the individual.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Today, eligible individuals with mental health conditions are given training allowance as they work on equipping themselves with skills to return to employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I share Ms Ng Ling Ling and Mr Sharael Taha's concerns that individuals with mental health conditions require stronger support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As highlighted by Mr Ong Hua Han, persons with disabilities need even greater help as they could be more vulnerable to mental health illnesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To this end, NCSS, together with the Beyond the Label Collective Workplace Workgroup members, is developing case studies and videos to increase awareness of best practices of inclusive employment and to guide employers on how to support employees when mental health issues arise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Employers may also refer to NCSS' Mental Health Toolkit on adjustments they may make for their individuals with mental health conditions, including having a phased return-to-work programme and providing a buddy or mentor.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: NCSS is also working with employment support agencies to develop a common framework to refer, assess and support individuals with varying readiness to return to work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Employees should be treated fairly and based on merit, even if they have chosen to disclose their mental health conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Government is committed to working with employers to strengthen support for employees' mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To the employers, we encourage you to tap on resources that are available.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To employees, let us strive to show kindness, support and understanding to those around us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Together, we can build a more inclusive society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I want to thank Dr Wan Rizal, Mr Edward Chia, Ms Mariam Jaafar, Dr Tan Wu Meng and Mr Yip Hon Weng for putting forward this Motion on advancing mental health and highlighting the need for a whole-of-Singapore effort to implement a national strategy to enhance mental health and well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I would also like to thank my colleagues who had just spoken, sharing on efforts in the health, social, education, workplace and community sectors; and many Members of Parliament, who have supported the various mental health initiatives and provided suggestions for improvements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I would also like to record my thanks to all the members of the task force, political office holders, people that we have consulted, community representatives, the Civil Service officers as well as the professionals that have contributed to not just the development of the strategy, but so much of what we have done since we launched the strategy to implement these programmes into action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: What is it that we are trying to do?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: What is it that we are trying to achieve?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As many colleagues have emphasised, mental health exists on a spectrum and requires a comprehensive approach involving the entire government and society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Instead of managing mental disorders only or solely, largely in hospital-based settings, the aim is to bring mental health support closer to individuals' everyday environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: By integrating care within the community, mental health support can be seamlessly delivered within natural social settings, such as schools and workplaces; and leveraging existing social and support networks, such as families, friends and coworkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: By shifting the focus of our efforts, the centre of gravity, into the community, by broadening the number of professions and processes that can be involved in mental health and by engaging larger and larger circles of the community, we are hoping to do a number of things in terms of changing what we do for mental health in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The first of many, I will just highlight three, but the first is increasing access to our mental health services ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We want to be able to make it easy for people to find the help that they need and access the touchpoints that will provide them the interventions that they will find useful.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The second, is to make sure that we make these interventions effective and certainly, for persons with mild mental health concerns or mental health conditions that are mild, care in the community, where they are able to continue to interact with their social circles, with their friends, with their family, with their workplace, have that normal routine of life, interventions in those settings may be more effective than removing the person from the natural rhythm of their life, institutionalising them and providing a very clinical response.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The third reason is that by involving a much wider variety of partners and more and more members of the community, we hope to be able to drive that shift in attitude that so many Members of this House have spoken about as being key to changing our approach towards mental health here in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: That is what we are trying to achieve and why we are trying to do this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: How we are doing so, I will go on to explain some of the details, and in particular, the tiered care model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This has been brought up by Senior Parliamentary of State Rahayu Mahzam.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It has been a central part of the strategy and has been discussed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I will highlight that this tiered care model is not something we need members of the public to internalise or use as a guide on how they seek services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Someone with mental health concerns does not need to look at the strategy and ask, "Am I a Tier 1?" That is not the point.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The tiered care model is an internal way of organising our services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is an internal way of thinking how we will invest the development of our services, shift the development of our professional capacity and capability, and integrate the various parts of our system with each other.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But the reason we explained it and, I will now explain it, is to make the point that we are very serious about what we want to do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are very serious about reorganising how we deliver our services and how we develop our capacity and our capability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, in explaining the breadth and depth of what we are doing, I will need to explain a little bit about how the tiered care model will be developed and implemented.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It will guide the delivery of our mental health services according to the severity of mental health needs and apply across a variety of settings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It serves as a framework, a foundation for strategic enhancements to our mental health ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Based on the severity of symptoms, individuals can tailor care according to their needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The majority of individuals, who may experience mental distress periodically without mental illness, could be best supported by peer supporters in schools or workplaces, as well as using self-help resources, including online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Overall, we aim to ensure that individuals with mental health needs receive the right support at the right time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This reflects a more nuanced and responsive approach to mental health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua shared about the Practice Guide that is being developed by the Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-Being together with key stakeholders from the health, social and education sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will translate the core concepts into practical steps to help practitioners effectively apply this tiered approach; make the framework work for their clients and for their patients; and enhance the integration and coordination of our mental health support system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have already put in place implementation teams, working groups and committees to execute our various plans and strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The processes in this Practice Guide will be piloted with some of the service providers and fine-tuned before being disseminated to mental health practitioners across our ecosystem by the end of the year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: GP clinics and polyclinics are important touchpoints for all of us, especially for individuals with mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They are community-based, easily accessible and we know that there is a strong association between physical and mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, the primary care service, primary care doctor and primary care clinic are ideally placed to treat the patient's physical and mental health conditions simultaneously and holistically.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These services at polyclinics are helmed by multi-disciplinary teams with family physicians, psychologists, medical social workers and nurses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In addition, over 450 GPs in GP clinics are trained to support persons with mental health needs under the Mental Health General Practitioner Partnership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Expanding mental health support in the community beyond healthcare settings is essential.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, 73 CREST work tirelessly to raise awareness, detect and refer individuals with mental health needs to the appropriate services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Eight of these teams currently cater to youths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The CREST teams work on awareness, detection and referrals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have another set of teams, which are the Community Intervention Teams (COMIT).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They provide mental health assessments and psychosocial interventions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, we have 29 of such teams, with four of them catering to youths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MOH is working with AIC to publicise these services as well, so that more people can benefit from access to these community-based mental health services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Other than expanding mental health services in primary and community care settings, we must also continue to ensure the safety and quality of services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I would point out that this space is not entirely a vacuum today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are, indeed, some regulatory processes and frameworks in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, services provided by clinical psychologists in healthcare institutions are subjected to the clinical governance framework of these healthcare institutions and existing healthcare legislations, such as the Healthcare Services Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In a non-healthcare setting, such as MSF-funded early intervention programmes, the operators do, indeed, employ mental health professionals, including clinical psychologists, to provide therapy services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These funding agreements for these services specify the minimum qualifications and training required before staff can be deployed to provide such services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, there are some regulatory frameworks in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But Members have made the point that perhaps it is insufficient for our situation today and, potentially, insufficient for the outcome of the shift that our national mental health strategy will engender.
