speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Psychology practice is evolving and already encompasses diverse fields with their own unique safety concerns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, MOH has been working already with agencies, service providers and professional associations to update the risk assessment and that updating of the risk assessment will have to take into account, then, what developments occur in the field in the near future; review and study these findings; and study the possible need to regulate clinical psychologists.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There is, I think, not a consensus among the suggestions within the House from which professions need what type of regulation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, we will study all the suggestions that are being made very seriously and look at these possibilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But beyond the regulation of clinical psychologists, building the competencies of other mental health practitioners and the community to effectively support individuals with mental health needs is another critical component of our strategy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, we have introduced the National Mental Health Competency Training Framework to enhance the capabilities of practitioners across the various tiers of care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This framework will complement existing professional standards for mental health professionals, such as psychologists and counsellors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It provides guidance to service providers in acquiring the necessary competencies which will then be aligned with the tiered care model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Importantly, this national mental health competency training framework is designed to be inclusive and it encompasses all practitioners and individuals involved in mental health support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, one single, national mental health competency training framework, from lay responders, like peer supporters, to mental health professionals, like psychologists and counsellors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As we step-up our capability building efforts, a substantial pool of peer supporters and service providers across Tiers 1, 2 and 3 will have the necessary baseline competencies to support individuals with mental health needs over the next two years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will equip a wide spectrum of practitioners and enhance the overall capability of the community to provide effective support for individuals with mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But we will also engage peer supporters and frontline personnel that are not within the healthcare and social space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They will be trained to identify mental health needs and provide psychological first aid, if needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Just as you do not need to be a healthcare worker to provide first aid, it is something that all of us can do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We want to train people to be able to provide psychological first aid, even if they are not a healthcare worker or a care professional.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, to have a broad network of support and individuals for mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: AIC has worked on this and put it online: awareness of the signs and symptoms of mental health conditions; and how to support individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They are accessible and open to the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are courses that you can go for psychological first aid.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, caregivers for individuals with mental health needs may also find it beneficial to participate in these courses and enhance their ability to care for their loved ones, the care recipients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The issue here is supporting individuals with mild symptoms of mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: How to identify the individuals, prevent an escalation of their symptoms and de-escalate a mental health crisis and formulating a safety plan for individuals with suicide risk.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Next to this, we have plans around what to do to support individuals with moderate symptoms of mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For that, service providers are trained to conduct mental health assessments and provide psychotherapy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, we distinguish those 130,000 frontline personnel and volunteers focused on mental health needs of people with mild conditions; and then a separate tier of interventions for individuals who can support people with mental health needs that are moderate in nature, with moderate symptoms – providing assessments, psychotherapy to reduce the severity of their symptoms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is part of our commitment to proactively upskill practitioners in the community to effectively support individuals with diverse mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Keith Chua, Ms Mariam Jaafar, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Vikram Nair highlighted concerns about persons with suicide risk.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The causes of suicide are multifaceted and it requires a holistic, multi-agency approach to address them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, in schools and IHLs, students at risk of suicide are supported by school counsellors, referred to REACH, Community Health Assessment Team (CHAT) or emergency services in hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: CareLine, a 24/7 social support hotline, provides tele-befriending as well as emergency response services to seniors in distress and it is operated by staff who can speak various dialects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Those in crisis can access crisis helplines, such as the Samaritans of Singapore's (SOS') Hotline and Care Text and IMH's Mental Health helpline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Under the National Mental Health Competency Training Framework, service providers in the community would be equipped with suicide risk assessment and intervention skills, so that individuals with suicide risk can be detected early and be provided with the relevant interventions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But we will continue to work on this and find ways to do what we do better and to make sure that every individual who needs help can find it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As a safety net to meet the care needs of individuals with severe and chronic mental health conditions, MOH will be expanding our hospital and our long-term care capacity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will be supported by plans to expand the pool of psychiatrists and psychologists in our public healthcare institutions, as has already been shared.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, the balance of that capacity increase will be different, depending on whether we are talking about inpatient psychiatric beds at places like IMH and the redeveloped Alexandra Hospital compared to, for example, long-term psychiatric care capacity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We hope that with all the things we are doing with our mental health strategy, while we will increase inpatient acute psychiatric capacity, the need for that will not be so significant because of the things we are doing upstream in the population and within the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But we will continue to need some increase in facilities in long-term psychiatric care capacity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, the balance is on the long-term residential psychiatric care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, even though we are expanding our capacity to provide mental health support for persons with severe mental health needs, it does not mean that we are adopting a purely medicalised approach towards mental health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There is room for non-medical interventions, such as art-based interventions, to play a bigger part in promoting mental well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To cultivate mental wellness, we need to live healthily.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: That means having friends, having adequate sleep, a healthy diet, taking part in sports, arts and volunteer work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These are not medical interventions, but they make a huge difference to an individual's life and a huge difference to an individual's health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The National Mental Health and Well-Being Strategy puts forth a comprehensive and holistic approach to addressing mental health issues across many different facets of society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It encompasses a preventive component as well as curative perspectives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We want to tackle the whole continuum of mental health issues coherently, with an emphasis on community, schools and workplace settings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We want to foster a whole-of-society approach, uniting efforts across different sectors to build a mentally healthy and resilient population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: After we launched the strategy last year, in late 2023, we have continued to engage with professionals and stakeholders in the space, and we have sought their feedback on the strategy and how the implementation was going.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: All of them supported the strategy recommendations, but consistently, all of them – professionals working in the mental healthcare space, whether they are healthcare workers or they are social workers in the community and within institutions – raised concerns about persistent stigma and the need for stronger partnerships.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The need for stronger partnerships between clients and providers, but also partnerships across different service providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is very important that we must not forget these fundamentals even as we talk about all the other things that we are doing around the implementation of the strategy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to address these issues as we go forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are many initiatives rolled out by the various Ministries and agencies to support individuals with mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ms Carrie Tan asked about the need to transition the current interagency task force to a permanent national well-being committee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Actually, these teams and officers have already begun work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They began work in supporting the work of the Inter-Ministry Taskforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They are the ones that worked together to put the strategy in place and they are already working together to implement our various programmes and recommendations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, the work will continue and the work is not done.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Members have highlighted issues that we have to continue to study, whether it is about the regulation of some professionals, issues to do with how insurance is made available and issues to do with stigma and access.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, we are quite clear that the work is not done and there is need for continued work in this space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The collective dedication and commitment of our Government agencies and the whole of our society are instrumental in driving positive change and fostering better mental health for all.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I was deeply moved by the stories and struggles shared in this Chamber.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In fact, I was crying when one of the stories was being shared about suicide.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Over the years, I have heard many, many stories.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: But to hear from Members, from each and every Member, shows how much we care for the communities we serve.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The voices of the Nominated Members of Parliament, with their unique insights and connections to the communities they serve, have been particularly striking.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Their contributions have not only enriched our debate but have also underscored the urgency of addressing mental health with compassion and action.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Mental health is everyone's business and I am glad that everyone agrees that business as usual is no longer acceptable.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The diversity of topics discussed, spanning different sectors and age groups, has highlighted our collective understanding that mental well-being cannot be compartmentalised.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In our spirited discussions over the last two days, we have delved deep into the myriad aspects of mental health, from increasing understanding and literacy to tackling the practicalities of cost, insurance and the critical support for caregivers.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Yet, amidst all these important conversations, one subject has notably stood out.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Touching the core of our humanity, shared by Dr Janil Puthucheary earlier as well, which is the stigma surrounding mental health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is profoundly personal, affecting individuals and families in every corner of our community.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The stigma mutes voices that need to be heard.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It isolates those who feel alone in their struggle and deepens the wounds of those silently suffering.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The story shared in our debate have underscored the urgent necessity to breakdown these walls of silence and isolation and our mission is clear to foster a society where conversations about mental health are met with open arms and understanding hearts, not judgement.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We need to cultivate an environment that encourages everyone to seek help about fear to talk openly without shame.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The mission spans across every facet of our society, from our schools to our workplaces, from our healthcare institutions to the very fabric of our communities.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Their journey of is one of love, resilience and, sometimes, silent struggle.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: They face their own set of challenges, bearing emotional and financial burdens, all while navigating the stigma associated with mental health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In one of my many conversations I had with the community, the caregivers often come forth and shared their challenges and hope that, through this strategy, our efforts would support them further.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The Government's response, led by Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, no less, is deeply appreciative and highly encouraging.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is a testament to our Government's unwavering commitment to advancing mental health care in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: But, more than policies and plans, the debate that we had, has been a powerful reminder of why we do what we do.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is about the people we serve, the lives we hope to improve and the community we wish to build.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: A Singapore where mental health is a priority for everyone.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The strategy that has been laid out is just the beginning.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is a promise of action, a roadmap towards a future where every Singaporean knows they are not alone in their struggles.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As we move forward, let us remember that our efforts today are for the long term.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The impact of our work might not be immediately visible, but we are planting seeds for a future where mental health is openly discussed, supported and prioritised.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As we look ahead, I invite every Member of this House to stand with us in this commitment.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is a pledge to our fellow Singaporeans that their well-being is our priority.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The journey may be long and challenging, but it is a journey worth taking together.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We are committing to a future where everyone feels supported, valued and understood.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Let us seize the opportunity to make a lasting difference in the lives of our people.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I urge you, Members of this House, to support this Motion, not just for the health of our nation but for the well-being of every individual who calls Singapore home.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: May our commitment and sustained efforts towards mental health last.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Together, we can and we will make mental health and well-being a reality for all.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Are there any clarifications for Dr Wan Rizal?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will be very happy to follow-up with her and other practitioners to look to see how we will engage with the practitioners, provide for an appropriate level of access, depending on the effectiveness of the various components of the intervention.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As has been brought up in the House, actually, Members have differing views as to how far regulation should go – which professions should be regulated, which interventions should be regulated, which settings should be regulated.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is something that we are studying and we will be very happy to study it together with the professionals involved in the space.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I am sorry I missed your hand just now, Ms Usha Chandradas.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Speaker, I would like to seek clarification from Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: When he articulated that the National Mental Health Office will continue to drive this effort, may I ask, whether it will be residing within MOH and, if so, how will the Prime Minister's Office ensure that the well-being initiatives and policies are well-coordinated across Ministries?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Because, for example, education policies will have an impact on manpower and manpower policies can have an impact on family life; and all these contribute to the levels of stress and bandwidth and all that.
